newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 2.4 pct, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 2.4 pct, but off highs.

text.p: Istanbul shares posted major gains in selective trade on Monday amid positive political expectations that the Islamist-led government will not be affected by a censure motion on Wednesday, brokers said.
But they fell from earlier highs on fresh resistance which emerged at the index's 78,500 level, they added.
The IMKB-100 closed up 1,805.11 points, or 2.37 percent at 78,015.62, down from an early high of 78,541. Trade volume rose to 16.7 trillion lira from 12.1 trillion on Friday.
"The market seems to have shaken off concerns about the government's future. It resumed the activity level seen early last week," said Sadi Aslangiray from Boyut securities.

The index had lost 4.2 percent in the last two days of last week after surging 22.7 percent from September 13 to last Wednesday's sixth consecutive all-time high close of 79,511.82 in a medium-term uptrend.

Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan who will be challenged in parliament after his recent controversial trip to Libya, told his party's Sunday congress that the government would work in harmony until the year 2000.
Brokers said purchases enlivened also because firm support of the index was confirmed at 76,000 during the down correction on Thursday and Friday.

Of the 225 shares traded, rises outdid falls sharply by 149 to 45 and 31 closed steady. The 85-share industrial index firmed 1.57 percent to 83,531.34 and the 15-share financial index surged 4.26 percent to 73,271.81.
Actives were led by cement pipe and brick producer Dogusan, UP 3,000 lira at 74,000, utilities Kepez Elektrik, up 2,000 lira at 86,000 and Aktas Elektrik, up 2,000 lira at 61,000.
